text.font-family: Encode Sans Expanded, Encode Sans, Arial, sans-serif

text.tspan: Ask me about this result. I can
only use what this analysis found.
Why does it feel like I’m
staying down when I’m not?
Because your chest stays bent over
while your hips move. In the
impact frame your hips are 7% of
your body height closer to the
ball than at address. Your upper
body has to rise to make room, but
your head and shoulders still feel
low, so it feels like staying
down.
Try the wall drill: if your
backside leaves the wall before
impact, you will feel the move the
video shows.
Should I change my grip
too?
This analysis didn’t measure your
grip, so I can’t say. A coach can
check it for you.
Answers are based only on this
analysis. Talk-back won’t invent
faults, numbers or drills.

svg.text: How do I know the drill is working?
Can I do this drill in a net?

text.tspan: Hips moved toward the ball by 7% of body height from address to impact. Fault threshold: 4%.

text.font-family: Encode Sans Expanded, Encode Sans, Arial, sans-serif

text.tspan: At address you set up well: hips back, chest over the ball. On the
way down your hips moved toward the ball, 7% of your body height by
impact. The rule table treats anything over 4% as early extension.
When the hips push forward, your chest has to lift to make room, and
your arms lose space to swing through. The likely reason is that your
lead hip isn’t turning enough: it had turned 31° at impact, where
about 45° is typical. If the hip can’t turn out of the way, it slides
toward the ball instead. So the job is to turn, not slide. The wall
drill teaches your hips to rotate while your backside stays back, and
the 90/90 hip rotation helps the hip turn more freely.

text.font-family: Encode Sans Expanded, Encode Sans, Arial, sans-serif

text.tspan: “It may feel like
you stay down, but
at impact your hips
have moved toward
the ball.”

svg.text: One drill for the fault, one mobility exercise for its likely cause.
Fig. 4 Trail glute on the wall

text.font-family: Encode Sans Expanded, Encode Sans, Arial, sans-serif

text.tspan: Set up with your backside
touching a wall, or your golf
bag. Make slow half swings,
keeping your trail glute on the
wall through impact.
If your backside comes off the
wall, your hips are moving toward
the ball.

text.font-family: Encode Sans Expanded, Encode Sans, Arial, sans-serif

text.tspan: Sit with both knees bent at
90°. Rotate slowly from one
side to the other, keeping
your chest tall.
Generic guidance, not medical advice — see a
physiotherapist if you feel pain.
